ordered_steps: Search customer by organization number via customer endpoint
If customer not found, create customer with name Sonnental GmbH and organization number 980215350
Search employee by email via employee endpoint
If employee not found, create employee for Emma Schneider with email emma.schneider@example.org
Create project via project endpoint with name "Analyse Sonnental"
Set project customer reference to Sonnental GmbH customer id
Set project manager reference to Emma Schneider employee id
Verify project creation and linked customer/project manager relations

planned_endpoints.summary: Create customer. Related customer addresses may also be created.

rules: When email is provided, ALWAYS set BOTH email AND invoiceEmail to the same value.
Do NOT send isCustomer (it's readOnly and auto-set).
For addresses, use postalAddress={addressLine1, postalCode, city, country={id: 161}} for Norway.
ALWAYS search first: GET /employee?email=<email> — the sandbox often has pre-existing employees. Reuse if found.
Only POST /employee if GET returns 0 results.
When POSTing, ALWAYS include department={"id": dept_id}. Create department first if needed.
userType should be 'STANDARD' unless admin is explicitly requested.
Requires customer={"id": customer_id} and projectManager={"id": employee_id}.
startDate is REQUIRED — use today_iso from execution_brief if prompt doesn't specify a date.
If a default hourly rate already exists (409 Duplicate entry), GET /project/hourlyRates?projectId=... then PUT to update it.

payload.trace_example_task: Create project with customer and project manager. 3-5 API calls.

payload.text:
Let me analyze the task:

1. Create project "Analyse Sonnental" linked to customer Sonnental GmbH (Org.-Nr. 980215350)
2. Project manager is Emma Schneider (emma.schneider@example.org)

Following the trace template:
1. POST /customer - create Sonnental GmbH
2. GET /employee?email=emma.schneider@example.org - check if employee exists
3. If not found, POST /department, then POST /employee
4. POST /project with name, customer, projectManager, startDate

Let me start with step 1 (create customer) and step 2 (check employee) in parallel.
I'll follow the trace template. First, I'll create the customer and check if the employee exists in parallel.
